world_frame.velocity_z_sign: POSITIVE UPWARD — OpenRocket TYPE_VELOCITY_Z is positive when ascending

body_frame.theta: Elevation angle of nose above horizontal (radians). theta=+pi/2 means nose straight up, theta=0 means nose horizontal, theta=-pi/2 means nose straight down

motor.thrust_axis_definition: Motor thrust acts along the rocket's positive longitudinal axis (nose direction)
motor.exhaust_direction: Exhaust exits opposite to thrust — toward the tail
motor.source: OpenRocket MotorMount ThrustVector — always aligned with rocket body-Z axis

kinematics.vertical_velocity_sign: POSITIVE when ascending, NEGATIVE when descending
kinematics.delta_velocity: Change in velocity vector over a time interval

alignment.q_vertical_formula: q_vertical = sin(theta) when vz < 0, -sin(theta) when vz >= 0
alignment.q_equals_plus_one_meaning: Nose axis is exactly opposite to velocity — full tail-first
alignment.q_equals_zero_meaning: Nose axis is perpendicular to velocity
alignment.q_equals_minus_one_meaning: Nose axis is aligned with velocity — full nose-first

critical_interpretation.during_tail_first_descent: Nose points upward (theta > 0), velocity points downward (vz < 0). Motor thrust is nose-directed (upward). Therefore thrust OPPOSES velocity — this is retrograde braking.
critical_interpretation.phase_2d_error: The Phase 2d test measured a rocket starting from rest on the launch pad. The +35.5 m/s velocity change was the rocket launching upward — expected behavior for a nose-directed motor. This does NOT prove the motor fires in the wrong direction during tail-first descent.
critical_interpretation.correct_conclusion: The motor fires in the correct direction (nose-directed). During tail-first descent, nose-directed thrust IS retrograde braking. The motor IS braking the stage.
